title: A platform-worker judgment can separate missing-pay correction from restored work control
source_unit: Federal Trade Commission and state enforcement case, court-entered order, and official Walmart Spark Driver payment FAQ; affected drivers are a remedy-program population, not a representative worker sample
geography: United States Walmart Spark Driver program; settlement relief is nationwide for eligible drivers

observations.period: February 26, 2026 complaint/settlement; March 3, 2026 court-entered order; payment and compliance status rechecked September 18, 2026

denominator.unit: eligible Spark Drivers with specified unpaid base-pay, tip, incentive, or promotion claims; complete denominator not published

direct_driver_allocation.unit: US dollars directed to drivers under the settlement distribution

ftc_driver_distribution_allocation.unit: US dollars Walmart pays to the FTC for intended driver distribution

state_civil_penalty_allocation.unit: US dollars paid as civil penalty to 11 participating states

payment_timing.value: Walmart began making payments to drivers in mid-2025 before the settlement announcement; the FAQ states these payments are included in the settlement

eligibility_scope.value: nationwide relief for drivers who accepted Spark delivery or shopping offers and did not receive promised base pay, tips, incentives, or promotions; not every driver will receive a payment

individual_payment_status.value: some drivers who already received payments should have emails stating payment dates; other drivers remain in identification/payment processing; aggregate sent, received, and unresolved counts are not published in the FAQ

later_work_and_exit.unit: missing continued work, alternative work, schedule/control, switching, trust, and exit endpoint

observations.method: Official FTC case page, court-entered order listing, complaint, settlement FAQ, and public payment/compliance description; court authority, allocation, pre-announcement payment timing, eligibility, and later work status are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The public materials do not disclose the complete eligible-driver denominator, individual payment amounts, payment receipt or dates for each driver, unresolved payment count, correction of driver records, continued platform work, alternative work, schedule control, recurrence, trust, or exit.
observations.subgroup: Drivers affected by alleged base-pay, tip, incentive, or promotion nonpayment; drivers who received pre-announcement payments; drivers still being identified; noneligible Spark Drivers; and drivers outside the participating states who remain eligible under the nationwide rule.
observations.counterinterpretation: A large ordered allocation and prospective earnings verification can correct monetary exposure without restoring the missed opportunity, schedule control, trust, or platform alternatives of each driver; a payment may compensate a past shortfall while the driver has already switched or stopped working.

related_sources.claim: FTC case page records the March 3, 2026 court-entered stipulated order and case identifiers.
Court-entered order establishes the $100 million judgment, driver and state allocations, injunction, and prospective compliance requirements.
Complaint describes alleged unpaid base pay, tips, incentives, and promotions in the Spark Driver program.

boundary: This record establishes a court-entered platform-worker remedy with explicit allocation, nationwide eligibility, pre-announcement payment timing, and a ten-year earnings-verification program. It does not establish the eligible-driver denominator, individual payment receipt, restored earnings opportunity, continued or alternative work, schedule control, trust, switching, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official FTC FAQ HTML route hashed; case page, complaint, and court-entered order routes reviewed without retaining the 16 MB order or respondent-level files
